subject: Ghanaian Language
name: JHS 1 Ghanaian Language
description: The JHS 1 Ghanaian Language curriculum aims to deepen learners' understanding and usage of their indigenous language. It covers customs and institutions, listening and speaking skills, reading comprehension, language structure and usage, composition writing, and literature.

strands.title: CUSTOMS AND INSTITUTIONS
strands.description: Understanding rites of passage, naming systems, clan systems, and chieftaincy.

subStrands.title: RITES OF PASSAGE - CHILDHOOD RITES
subStrands.description: Exploring childhood rites and naming ceremonies.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the childhood rites of their culture and compare with other Ghanaian cultures

indicators.description: Identify the processes involved in naming a child

exemplars.description: Discuss the outdooring and the naming process of a child in their community (e.g., outdooring/ushering the baby, invitation of ancestors, giving the baby a name, blessing, presentation of gifts).
Identify the items used in the naming process and write them (e.g., water, basket, bucket, beads, basin, mat, powder, lantern, clothes).
Explain the significance of the items used for the naming ceremony.

indicators.description: Discuss the significance of the processes in naming a child

exemplars.description: Read a passage on naming ceremony in their culture.
Discuss the significance of the processes involved in naming a child (e.g., welcomes the child into the family/community, child gets an identity).
Discuss a libation text used during naming ceremony.
Write the three main parts of a libation text.

indicators.description: Compare and contrast the naming processes in their culture to other Ghanaian cultures

exemplars.description: Discuss the naming process of one other culture of Ghana and compare with the naming process of their people.
Write about commonalities and differences among the cultures.

indicators.description: Compare and contrast the traditional naming process to the contemporary naming process

exemplars.description: Discuss the contemporary naming processes and compare it with the traditional naming processes in Ghana.
Show the similarities (e.g., organized, family involvement, gifts) and differences (e.g., venue, items used, timing).

indicators.description: Role play a naming ceremony session in their culture

exemplars.description: Role play a naming ceremony among their people.
Discuss the role play and what they have learnt from it.

subStrands.title: NAMING SYSTEMS: DAY NAMES, ORDER OF BIRTH NAMES
subStrands.description: Understanding naming based on days and birth order.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit understanding of day-born names and order of birth names and relate the names to the days and order of birth

indicators.description: State the names of the days of the week and relate their names to the days

exemplars.description: State the names of the days of the week and important occasions/months.
Relate the names of the days of the week or months to human names (e.g., Akan: Monday - Adwoa/Kwadwo).

indicators.description: State the order of birth (i.e. first, second, and so on.) and relate the names accordingly

exemplars.description: State the order of birth of their culture.
Relate the names to the order of birth (e.g., First born: Piesie (Akan), Tete (Dangme)).

indicators.description: Compare and contrast the day names and order of birth names in their culture to other cultures in Ghana

exemplars.description: Compare the day names and order of birth names in their culture with those of other cultures.
Discuss the similarities and differences.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the clan system among their people

indicators.description: Describe the clan system and state some clans in their ethnic community

exemplars.description: Explain what a clan is.
State some clans you know (e.g., Akan: Aduana, Agona; Ga: Sempe, Kinkawe).

indicators.description: Discuss the features of the clan system in relation to their community

exemplars.description: Discuss the features of their clan system (e.g., symbols, taboos, totems, names).
Relate their clan system to another clan system.
Read a passage on a clan system.
Write the main ideas in the passage read in their own words.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge in and an understanding of how chiefs and queenmothers are selected, enstooled/enskinned and compare their duties and responsibilities

indicators.description: Discuss how chiefs and queenmothers are selected in their ethnic community

exemplars.description: Read a passage on how chiefs and queenmothers are selected.
Identify the traditional leaders mentioned in the passage.
Relate how chiefs and queenmothers are selected among their people to the passage.

indicators.description: Discuss the processes involved in enstooling/enskinning chiefs and queenmothers

exemplars.description: Discuss the qualities of a person who qualifies to be a chief or queenmother.
Create a profile of the qualities of a chief or queenmother.
Identify those who select the chief and queenmother.
Role play the enstoolment/enskinment of chiefs and queenmothers.

indicators.description: Discuss the duties and responsibilities of chiefs and queenmothers among their people

exemplars.description: Identify the duties of a chief and queenmother in their community.
Evaluate the duties of a chief and queenmother among your people.

indicators.description: Discuss and compare modern trends affecting the enstoolment/enskinment of chiefs and queenmothers

exemplars.description: Discuss some modern trends affecting enstoolment/enskinment (e.g., Monetary influence, political influence).
Explain how the trends mentioned affect the chieftaincy institution.
Compare the modern ways of enstooling/enskinning with traditional ways.

subStrands.title: CONVERSATION/EVERYDAY DISCOURSE
subStrands.description: Using appropriate language in various contexts.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate use of appropriate language orally in specific situations

indicators.description: Use appropriate register in everyday communication (informal and formal) with diverse partners on grade-level topics/texts/issues

exemplars.description: Identify formal situations (e.g. interactions between strangers, announcements).
Use appropriate language to participate in formal interactions.
Identify informal situations.
Use appropriate language to participate in informal conversations.

indicators.description: Ask questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others' questions in a conversation

exemplars.description: Identify words that can help give elaborate responses (e.g. why, how).
Engage in conversation using these words to elicit elaboration.

indicators.description: Use appropriate language orally to describe experiences about oneself and others

exemplars.description: Use appropriate language (tense structures, figurative expressions) to describe experiences.
Use appropriate vocabulary to talk about experiences in specific situations.

indicators.description: Listen to and give accurate directions to familiar places

exemplars.description: Use appropriate language and landmarks to show direction.
Direct people using vocabulary appropriately.

indicators.description: Use techniques (voice modulation and eye contact) for effective oral communication

exemplars.description: Converse using appropriate voice.
Maintain eye contact.
Engage in conversation using right tone and eye contact.

subStrands.title: LISTENING COMPREHENSION
subStrands.description: Listening skills for understanding key information.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the ability to listen to extended reading and identify key information

indicators.description: Listen to a level-appropriate text attentively and identify key information

exemplars.description: Identify key points (intent, speaker's enthusiasm, main ideas).
Read out and cross check information.

indicators.description: Listen to, discuss ideas and share opinions from a level-appropriate text

exemplars.description: Listen to and write key points.
Discuss key points and share opinions.

subStrands.title: SPEECH SOUNDS - VOWELS, CONSONANTS AND SYLLABLES

contentStandards.description: Recognise and sound vowels and consonants and read one syllable words of their linguistic community

indicators.description: Identify and produce the vowels in the language of study

exemplars.description: Identify vowels in words.
Produce the vowel sounds.
Record the vowel sounds.
Pronounce vowel sounds correctly in connected speech.

indicators.description: Identify and produce the consonants in the language of study

exemplars.description: Identify consonants in words.
Produce consonant sounds.
Record consonant sounds.
Pronounce consonant sounds correctly in connected speech.

indicators.description: Identify and produce one to four syllable words of the language of study

exemplars.description: Read one syllable words.
Read two to three syllable words.
Read four syllable words.
Pronounce polysyllabic words correctly.

subStrands.title: TONE
subStrands.description: Understanding basic tones in the language.

contentStandards.description: Recognise the basic tones in their language

indicators.description: Identify and produce the basic tones in their language

exemplars.description: Identify tones on syllables.
Pronounce words with tones correctly.
Use knowledge of tone to pronounce same words with different tones.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit an understanding of recognising and producing words and using them in sentences

indicators.description: Identify and produce words in the home and school environments and use them to form meaningful sentences

exemplars.description: Identify vocabulary items in relation to the home.
Identify vocabulary items in relation to the school.
Use vocabularies to form sentences.

contentStandards.description: Present information effectively on familiar topics using appropriate language

indicators.description: Describe daily activities using appropriate register, structure and gestures for the contest being presented

exemplars.description: Outline daily activities.
Narrate daily activities with gestures.
Develop a daily activity calendar.
Converse with others about daily activities.
Make a presentation on other familiar topics.

subStrands.title: READING
subStrands.description: Understanding main ideas and summarising texts.

contentStandards.description: Understand the main ideas and supporting points in texts

indicators.description: Read and understand main ideas and supporting points in a range of texts on familiar and unfamiliar topics

exemplars.description: Skim a passage and state main ideas.
Identify supporting ideas in texts from other subject areas.
Explain relationship between main and supporting ideas.
Answer recall and inferential questions.

indicators.description: Read to understand and summarise the main ideas in a given grade level passage

exemplars.description: Identify and write main ideas.
List ideas in order.
Summarise a passage in own words.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of translating words, phrases and simple sentences

indicators.description: Translate words and phrases in his/her language

exemplars.description: Translate given words and simple phrases from source to target language.
Translate phrases/simple sentences from source to target language.
Translate simple sentences from source to target language.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the components of sentences

indicators.description: Discuss the components of sentences

exemplars.description: Explain what a sentence is.
Give examples of sentences and component parts.
Discuss components of a sentence.

indicators.description: Discuss the types of sentence structure (simple, compound and complex)

exemplars.description: Identify components of a simple sentence and give examples.
Identify components of a compound sentence and give examples.
Identify components of a complex sentence and give examples.

indicators.description: Classify sentences according to functions (declarative, imperative and interrogative)

exemplars.description: Identify functions of a sentence.
Construct sentences in relation to functions.

subStrands.title: INTEGRATING GRAMMAR IN WRITTEN LANGUAGE (NOUNS, PRONOUNS AND ADJECTIVES)
subStrands.description: Using nouns, pronouns, and adjectives correctly.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of identifying and using the various forms of nouns (common, proper, collective), pronouns and adjectives in sentences and passages

indicators.description: Categorise nouns under common, proper and collective and use them correctly in speech and in texts

exemplars.description: Identify nouns in passages.
Classify nouns.
Pronounce and use nouns correctly.
Construct sentences with nouns.

indicators.description: Categorise pronouns according to their types and construct sentences with them

exemplars.description: Identify pronouns.
Classify pronouns.
Construct sentences with pronouns.
Replace nouns with pronouns.

indicators.description: Categorise adjectives into their types and construct simple sentences with them

exemplars.description: Identify adjectives.
Classify adjectives.
Use adjectives to form sentences.

subStrands.title: INTEGRATING GRAMMAR IN WRITTEN LANGUAGE (VERBS, ADVERBS, CONJUNCTIONS, POSTPOSITIONS/PREPOSITIONS)
subStrands.description: Using verbs, adverbs, conjunctions, and postpositions/prepositions correctly.

contentStandards.description: Recognise the use of verbs, adverbs, conjunctions and postpositions/Prepositions in sentences

indicators.description: Identify and classify verbs into their types

exemplars.description: Identify and use verbs appropriately.
Categorise verbs and use them to construct sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and classify adverbs into their various types

exemplars.description: Identify and use adverbs appropriately.
Categorise adverbs and use them to construct sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and classify conjunctions and use them appropriately in a range of texts

exemplars.description: Identify and use conjunctions appropriately.
Categorise conjunctions and use them to construct sentences.

indicators.description: Explore the use of postpositions/prepositions appropriately and correctly in a range of texts

exemplars.description: Identify and use postpositions/prepositions appropriately in sentences.

subStrands.title: VOCABULARY, SPELLING AND PUNCTUATION
subStrands.description: Applying vocabulary, spelling, and punctuation correctly.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of vocabulary, spelling and punctuations in writing

indicators.description: Use vocabulary appropriately and correctly in writing

exemplars.description: Identify and write vocabulary related to home and school.
Use vocabulary to construct sentences.

indicators.description: Spell words related to home and school correctly

exemplars.description: Write down dictated vocabulary items.
Construct sentences with vocabulary items.

indicators.description: Identify and use punctuations appropriately and correctly in writing

exemplars.description: Use punctuation marks appropriately in a paragraph.

strands.title: COMPOSITION WRITING
strands.description: Structuring and organizing ideas in writing.

subStrands.title: STRUCTURE AND ORGANISE IDEAS IN COMPOSITION WRITING

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the features of a paragraph and the various text types (narrative, descriptive, creative/free writing)

indicators.description: Discuss the features of a paragraph

exemplars.description: Write topic and supporting sentences.
Organise ideas in paragraphs.
Identify salient points in a paragraph.
Write a paragraph on a given topic.

indicators.description: Develop a three-paragraph essay using the features of a given text type

exemplars.description: Discuss features of narrative, descriptive, creative/free writing.
Write a three-paragraph essay on a topic.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the knowledge and understanding of literature (Oral and Written)

indicators.description: Discuss the components of literature

exemplars.description: Discuss characteristics of literature.
Classify literature into types.
Give examples and relate to types.
Develop skills of appreciating and analysing texts.

indicators.description: Discuss the components of oral literature (folktales and songs-lullabies and play songs)

exemplars.description: Explain what oral literature is.
Describe structure of a folktale and a song.
Analyse a folktale and a song.
Appreciate significance of folktale and song.

indicators.description: Discuss the components of written literature (prose, drama and poetry)

exemplars.description: Discuss structure of genres.
Discuss character creation.
Explore literary devices, mood, and tone.
